questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.8]\coordinate (A) at (0,0);\coordinate (B) at (3.5,0);\coordinate (C) at (0,2.5);\draw (A)--(B) node[midway,below] {$g$};\draw (A)--(C) node[midway,left] {$h$};\draw (B)--(C) node[midway,above right] {$k$};\coordinate (va) at ($(A)!0.3cm!(B)$);\coordinate (vb) at ($(A)!0.3cm!(C)$);\draw (va)--($(va)+(vb)-(A)$)--(vb);\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Which side is the hypotenuse?

options.why: Chose a shorter side (a leg) that meets the right angle instead of the side opposite it.
Assumed the bottom horizontal side is always the hypotenuse.

questions.solution_text: The hypotenuse is $k$, the side opposite the right angle.

questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.8]\coordinate (J) at (0,3.2);\coordinate (L) at (-2.4,1.4);\coordinate (K) at (2.4,0);\draw (J)--(L) node[midway,above left] {$e$};\draw (J)--(K) node[midway,above right] {$f$};\draw (L)--(K) node[midway,below] {$g$};\coordinate (va) at ($(J)!0.3cm!(L)$);\coordinate (vb) at ($(J)!0.3cm!(K)$);\draw (va)--($(va)+(vb)-(J)$)--(vb);\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
The right angle is at the top vertex. Which side is the hypotenuse?

options.why: Picked a slanted leg forming the right angle at the top, not the side opposite it.
Picked the other slanted leg forming the right angle rather than the opposite side.

questions.solution_text: The hypotenuse is $g$, the side opposite the right angle at the top vertex.

questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.8]\coordinate (A) at (0,0);\coordinate (B) at (4.5,0);\coordinate (C) at (0,2);\draw (A)--(B) node[midway,below] {$12$};\draw (A)--(C) node[midway,left] {$5$};\draw (B)--(C) node[midway,above right] {$13$};\coordinate (va) at ($(A)!0.3cm!(B)$);\coordinate (vb) at ($(A)!0.3cm!(C)$);\draw (va)--($(va)+(vb)-(A)$)--(vb);\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Which side length is the hypotenuse?

options.why: Chose the longer leg instead of the side opposite the right angle.
Chose the shortest side rather than the longest side, the hypotenuse.

questions.solution_text: $13$, the side opposite the right angle and the longest side.

questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.9]\coordinate (A) at (0,0);\coordinate (R) at (0,1.6);\coordinate (E) at (3,0);\draw (A)--(R) node[midway,left] {rise};\draw (A)--(E) node[midway,below] {ground};\draw (R)--(E) node[midway,above right] {ramp};\coordinate (va) at ($(A)!0.3cm!(E)$);\coordinate (vb) at ($(A)!0.3cm!(R)$);\draw (va)--($(va)+(vb)-(A)$)--(vb);\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
A wheelchair ramp rises from the ground to a raised doorway, forming a right angle between the vertical rise and the ground. Which length is the hypotenuse?

options.text: The sloping length of the ramp
The horizontal distance across the ground
options.why: This is a shorter side along the ground, a leg that meets the right angle, not the side opposite it.

options.text: The vertical height of the rise
options.why: This is the other leg, running up to the right angle, not the side opposite it.

questions.solution_text: The ramp is the hypotenuse, the side opposite the right angle between the rise and the ground.

\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.8]\coordinate (A) at (0,0);\coordinate (B) at (2.2,1.1);\coordinate (C) at (-1.1,2.2);\draw (A)--(B) node[midway,below right] {$p$};\draw (A)--(C) node[midway,left] {$q$};\draw (B)--(C) node[midway,above right] {$t$};\coordinate (va) at ($(A)!0.3cm!(B)$);\coordinate (vb) at ($(A)!0.3cm!(C)$);\draw (va)--($(va)+(vb)-(A)$)--(vb);\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
This right-angled triangle is drawn on a slant with the right angle at the left. Which side is the hypotenuse?

options.why: Picked a leg meeting the right angle because the triangle is rotated, not the opposite side.
Picked the other leg at the right angle instead of the side opposite it.

questions.solution_text: The hypotenuse is $t$, the side opposite the right angle at $A$.
